title: Relative/inferior adoration does not clear Rome—Protestants never charged absolute god-cult of images
source_text: IV. Nec est quod dicant adorationem quam deferunt imaginibus non esse summam & absolutam illam, quam soli Deo deberi agnoscunt; neque se habere imagines pro Diis, sed eas colere tantum adoratione quadam inferiori, quae ad Prototypa refertur. Etenim quum Protestantes Ecclesiam Romanam incusant ut adorantem imagines, nolunt Ecclesiae Romanae tribuere quod Imagines pro Diis habeat, adeoque quod imagines colat alia adoratione quam relativa, & quae sit infra summam. Quin ab eo tantum absunt, ut ne quidem ipsis Ethnicis, cordatioribus saltem & non plane stupidis, simile quid citra injuriam tribui posse arbitrentur: cum eorum sapientes & Philosophi saepius declarent se lapideas aut ligneas imagines Deos non existimare; nec se alia mente eas colere, quam ut in iis, & per eas honorem deferant iis numinibus, quorum ipsae sunt signa & simulacra. Cum ergo Protestantes non alio modo credant & dicant imagines ab Ecclesia Romana adorari, quam eo quem ipsa probat & profitetur, planum est eos hac in parte, nihil illi per calumniam imputare.
pass_a_gloss: Nor is there reason for them to say that the adoration which they pay to images is not that highest and absolute adoration which they acknowledge to be due to God alone; nor that they hold images for Gods, but cultivate them only with a certain inferior adoration, which is referred to the Prototypes. For when Protestants accuse the Roman Church as adoring images, they do not wish to attribute to the Roman Church that she holds Images for Gods, and accordingly that she cultivates images with an adoration other than relative, and which is below the highest. Nay, they are so far from that, that they judge that not even to the Gentiles themselves, at least the more discerning and not plainly stupid, can the like be attributed without injury: since their wise men and Philosophers often declare that they do not reckon stone or wooden images to be Gods; nor that they cultivate them with any other mind than that in them, and through them, they may pay honor to those divinities of whom they themselves are signs and simulacra. Since therefore Protestants believe and say that images are adored by the Roman Church in no other mode than that which she herself approves and professes, it is plain that in this part they impute nothing to her by calumny.
pass_b_english: Rome’s refuge—only relative, inferior adoration—is the very thing Protestants meant.
Even thoughtful pagans denied their statues were gods; Protestants do not charge Rome with that stupidity.
So the accusation tracks Rome’s own relative cult, not a forged absolute one.
